extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, DHS/USCIS adjudicators, policy stakeholders, and noncitizen applicants/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining which nonimmigrant and adjustment-of-status applicants are subject to the proposed public-charge condition (proposed 8 CFR provisions), what forms they must file, and how USCIS will evaluate public-charge inadmissibility in the adjustment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to apply for Extension of Stay / Change of Status (form filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table header: "Eligible to apply for Extension of Stay (i.e. May File Form I-129 or Form I-539)" and "Eligible to apply for Change of Status (i.e. May File Form I-129 or I-Form 539)". The table records "Yes" or "No" for each nonimmigrant classification and cites the controlling INA/8 CFR/22 CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the alien must file an I-129 or an I-539 depends on the status the alien is applying to change to or extend; table entries cite the relevant statutory/regulatory provision (e.g., 8 CFR citations, INA sections) for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject to Public Benefit Condition under proposed 8 CFR provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Table column: "Subject to Public Benefit Condition under proposed 8 CFR 214.1(a)(3)(iv), 214.1(a)(4)(iv); 248.1(c)(4)" indicating, for each nonimmigrant class, whether that class is subject to the proposed public-benefits condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table lists many specific nonimmigrant classes (e.g., N-8, N-9, NATO-1..7, O-1..O-3, P-1..P-4, Q-1, R-1..R-2, etc.) with "Yes" or "No" entries and cites statutory/regulatory authorities (INA, 8 CFR, 22 CFR) to support applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms I-129/I-539 and I-944 procedural questions about public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: "*Includes questions on Form I-129 and Form I-539 about previous applications for or receipt of public benefits, and applicant may be required to File Form I-944 if requested by USCIS."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note that the listed nonimmigrant filings include questions about prior applications/receipt of public benefits; USCIS may request Form I-944 (Declaration of Self-Sufficiency) from applicants where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of Status eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Text: "In general, an alien who is physically present in the United States may be eligible to apply for adjustment of status before USCIS to that of a lawful permanent resident if the applicant was inspected and admitted or paroled, is eligible to receive an immigrant visa, is admissible to the United States, and has an immigrant visa immediately available at the time of filing the adjustment of status application."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS is responsible for determining the applicant's burden of proof on eligibility; aliens in removal proceedings may also apply pursuant to 8 CFR 1245. The adjustment process includes assessing whether any inadmissibility grounds in section 212(a) apply and whether a waiver is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS evaluation standard for public-charge inadmissibility (totality of circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text: "In determining whether the adjustment applicant has demonstrated that he or she is not inadmissible on the public charge ground, DHS proposes to review the mandatory statutory factors together with any required affidavit of support and any other relevant information, in the totality of the circumstances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation will consider mandatory statutory factors (those identified in statute), any submitted affidavit(s) of support (e.g., Form I-864), and other relevant evidence; decision is made under a totality-of-the-circumstances standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) and the requirement to file Form I-944 for family-based adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 5: "Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) to Family-Based Adjustment of Status Applications" with a column "Subject to INA 212(a)(4) and must file Form I-944, Declaration of Self-Sufficiency?*" showing "Yes" or "No" by category (Immediate Relatives, Family-Based Preferences, Fiancé K-1/K-2, Amerasians, VAWA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table specifies for each family-based category whether INA 212(a)(4) applies and whether the applicant must file Form I-944; footnotes explain numerous statutory exceptions (e.g., applicants who filed I-485 prior to Dec. 19, 1997; certain Amerasian and VAWA categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: INA 213A and Form I-864 Affidavit of Support: required or exempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Table columns indicate for each adjustment category whether "INA 213A and Form I-864, Affidavit of Support Required or Exempt?" (e.g., Required, Exempt, Not Applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes detail when the affidavit requirement is inapplicable or exempt (examples: some Amerasian categories, VAWA exemptions, many special immigrant categories where the 'employer' is not a qualifying relative or for-profit entity). Citations to INA and 8 CFR provided for each determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-charge bond option (Form I-945) and cancellation (Form I-356)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text/footnote: "If found inadmissible based on the public charge ground, USCIS, at its discretion, may permit the alien to post a public charge bond (Form I-945). A public charge bond may be cancelled (Form I-356) upon the death, naturalization (or otherwise obtaining U.S. citizenship), permanent departure of the alien, or otherwise as outlined in proposed 8 CFR 213.1(g), if the alien did not receive any public benefits as defined in the proposed rule."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public-charge-bond mechanism is discretionary; cancellation conditions and additional rules (e.g., cancellation upon the fifth anniversary in some contexts) are described elsewhere in the proposed regulation and accompanying tables/footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) to employment-based adjustment and ownership-interest exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 6: "Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) to Employment-Based Adjustment of Status Applications" lists preferences (First, Second, Third, Fifth/EB-5) and marks whether subject to INA 212(a)(4) and must file I-944. The table also shows whether INA 213A/Form I-864 is required or exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment-based applicants generally are subject to INA 212(a)(4) (Yes). The affidavit-of-support requirement is exempt unless there is a qualifying relative or an entity in which such a relative has a significant ownership interest (5% or more) in the filed Form I-140 (see 8 CFR 213a.1). Footnotes clarify EB-5 and other special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) to Special Immigrant categories and category-specific exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 7: "Applicability of INA 212(a)(4) to Special Immigrant Adjustment of Status Application" lists many EB-4/special-immigrant subclasses (religious workers, international employees of USG abroad, Panama Canal employees, foreign medical grads, retired G-4 employees, SIJ, US Armed Forces personnel, international broadcasters, special immigrant interpreters, etc.) and whether they are subject to INA 212(a)(4) and whether INA 213A/Form I-864 is required or exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many special-immigrant subclasses are subject to INA 212(a)(4) but the affidavit-of-support requirement is often 'Not Applicable' because the employer generally would not be a qualifying relative or a for-profit entity. Specific statutory exemptions are noted (e.g., SIJ are exempt under INA 245(h); special immigrant interpreters for Iraq/Afghanistan are statutorily exempt by specified NDAA provisions). Footnotes cite the controlling statutes and regulations for each listed category.
